title: New Lagos Rising Revisited
premise: Ines Montrose, navigator of the freighter Halcyon Drift, has spent six years ferrying supplies to New Lagos, a colony the war between Earth's Compact and the Belt Concord has quietly abandoned. The ship's hold carries illegal neural backups of dead colonists, including Ines's own previous self, a secret that makes them complicit in the very identity crimes they despise. When gravity across the system stutters for nine seconds, Ines realizes someone is testing a weapon that could crack every colony world at once — and that the message needed to stop it is encoded in the backups sleeping in their own hold. To deliver it, Ines must expose themselves, their crew, and the truth about who really ordered New Lagos forgotten, choosing loyalty to the living over loyalty to the dead.
about_author: I. M. Blackwood is the pen name of a former merchant marine radio officer who claims to have logged more hours listening to dead channels than live ones. They write from an undisclosed coastal town, where they keep a telescope pointed at the sea instead of the sky.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Silence
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, mid-run to New Lagos, when gravity flickers for exactly nine seconds and every instrument lies at once. The crew laughs it off; Ines cannot. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine, the first crack in a world Ines thought was stable.

chapters.title: The Hold That Dreams
chapters.summary: Ines descends into the backup hold during night cycle, speaking aloud to the sleeping copies, especially 'Ines Prime,' dead three years. POV: Ines. Establishes the illegal backups and the guilt binding Ines to them. Emotional beat: tenderness curdling into shame.

chapters.title: Cargo for a Ghost Town
chapters.summary: Docking at New Lagos, where the population has halved since last visit and Governor Adeyemi pretends otherwise. POV shifts to dockmaster Sefu Okafor, who falsifies census data out of loyalty. Emotional beat: quiet grief of being forgotten by everyone but each other.

chapters.title: What the Tides Remember
chapters.summary: Sefu shows Ines the colony's tidal records: the nine-second flicker left physical scars in the water table. Someone measured it before it happened. POV: Sefu. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing you were never invisible, only unwatched.

chapters.title: Crew Manifest
chapters.summary: Back aboard, engineer Dara Voss catches Ines near the hold and reveals she's known about the backups for a year and said nothing. POV: Dara. Loyalty vs. truth begins its war inside the crew. Emotional beat: relief and betrayal arriving in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Compact's Long Arithmetic
chapters.summary: A Compact patrol vessel hails the Drift with questions too precise to be routine. Ines lies beautifully and hates how good they've become at it. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: the cost of survival measured in small corruptions.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: Sefu uncovers sealed colonial archives proving New Lagos was deliberately struck from supply schedules — a bureaucratic execution. POV: Sefu. He asks Ines to carry the evidence out. Emotional beat: righteous fury tempered by fear no one will listen.

chapters.title: Gravity Is a Language
chapters.summary: Dara reverse-engineers the flicker: it was a handshake protocol, a test broadcast aimed at the colony's old deep-space array. Someone expected an answer. POV: Dara. Emotional beat: exhilaration shadowed by the question of who else is listening.

chapters.title: The Second Copy
chapters.summary: Ines wakes one of the backups briefly — Ines Prime — inside a jury-rigged interface. The conversation is brutal: Prime calls Ines a coward hiding behind other people's secrets. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: confronting the self you fled from.

chapters.title: Concord in the Dark
chapters.summary: A Belt Concord stealth ship shadows the Drift; its captain, Wren Ilyich, offers asylum for the archive data. She knows about the backups somehow. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: charm as a weapon, and the loneliness beneath it.

chapters.title: Divided Course
chapters.summary: Crew council: give the archives to the Compact, the Concord, or no one. Dara wants truth published; Sefu's proxy argues for leverage. Ines abstains, and the abstention costs them trust. POV: rotating crew voices. Emotional beat: a family discovering its fault lines.

chapters.title: New Lagos Rising (Reprise)
chapters.summary: The colony, learning it was erased on purpose, erupts into organized refusal — work stoppages, open broadcasts. Sefu becomes its reluctant voice. POV: Sefu. Emotional beat: hope as an act of defiance, fragile and loud.

chapters.title: Interdiction
chapters.summary: The Compact blockades New Lagos to contain the broadcasts. The Drift is caught in the cordon; Wren's Concord ship offers cover at a price: the backups as proof of Compact identity-crimes. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: every exit now runs through betrayal.

chapters.title: The Message in the Dead
chapters.summary: Dara decrypts the flicker's handshake fully: it was addressed using authentication keys that exist only in the colonists' neural backups — the weapon test was also a search for them. POV: Dara. Emotional beat: horror at understanding, finally, why the colony was forgotten: it was quarantined around a secret.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds, Again
chapters.summary: A second, longer gravity flicker strikes — a countdown made physical. Structures fail on New Lagos; Sefu is injured saving children from the collapsing seawall. POV: Sefu. Emotional beat: sacrifice without guarantee, love as infrastructure.

chapters.title: Wren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wren corners Ines: hand over the backups or she takes them. But her own logs reveal the Concord authorized the original quarantine. Neither side is clean. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: a true believer watching her faith die in real time.

chapters.title: What Ines Prime Knew
chapters.summary: Ines wakes Prime again, permanently this time, and learns the truth: Prime helped build the encryption keys and chose death over surrendering them. The message ending the war was written by the dead, entrusted to the living. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: inheritance, forgiveness, terror of the task.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax part one: the Drift runs the blockade while Dara transmits the decrypted message — proof of the weapon, the quarantine order, and both governments' signatures — on all bands. POV: Ines at the helm. Emotional beat: total exposure as the only honest act left.

chapters.title: Crossfire at the Lighthouse Array
chapters.summary: Climax part two: Compact and Concord ships converge on the transmitter. Wren defects, shielding the Drift with her own hull. Sefu, wounded, keys the final authentication from the colony's end. POV: alternating Ines/Wren/Sefu. Emotional beat: three loyalties converging into one truth.

chapters.title: Ceasefire, Conditional
chapters.summary: Both fleets stand down as the broadcast goes galactic; inquiries begin, and the architects of the quarantine are named. But the colonies demand more than words. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: exhausted vindication that tastes like ash.

chapters.title: Resting State
chapters.summary: Resolution: the surviving backups are offered legal personhood hearings; Ines must testify beside their own dead self. Prime chooses to remain archived rather than be restored, freeing Ines to live unshadowed. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: grief resolved into gratitude.

chapters.title: New Lagos Rising, Unrevised
chapters.summary: Epilogue: one year later, New Lagos thrives as the war's moral center; the Drift takes a new contract — carrying colonists home. Ines navigates by choice, not hiding. Final line echoes the opening flicker, now read as a heartbeat. Emotional beat: arrival, and the courage to be seen.
